{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>It ''[the Belascoan Archive Report]'' details Hutt-backed assaults on five different worlds beyond what was then the frontier: Lexrul, Drogheda, Hathrox, Imram&hellip;and Parcovey Minor.|Thunys Albegron, Proceedings of the Obroa-Skai Conference on Popular Entertainment|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
'''Imram''' was a [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] located within [[Lannik Space/Legends|Lannik Space]]. During the [[Kymoodon Era]], [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] settled Imram, which members of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]] viewed as an act of war.

As a result, the Hutts sponsored [[Assault on Imram|raids on Imram]] and other Republic colonies, leading to the [[Slavery/Legends|enslavement]] or [[Death/Legends|death]] of many colonists. The events on Imram were recorded in a [[Belascoan Archive Report|report]] that eventually came to rest in a [[Kymoodon-era government archive|government archive]] on the planet [[Belasco/Legends|Belasco]].

==Description==
Imram was a [[Planet/Legends|world]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> located in the [[Imram system/Legends|Imram system]]. It was part of the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] known as [[Lannik Space/Legends|Lannik Space]], within the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]]<ref name="EAOC" /> and [[The Slice/Legends|the Slice]] regions.<ref name="Slice" />

==History==
{{Quote|<nowiki></nowiki>''[&hellip;]'' the threats faced in the Kymoodon Era by Republic colonists were far from imaginary.|Thunys Albegron, Proceedings of the [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-Skai]] Conference on Popular Entertainment|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Lannikspace.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Imram was located in Lannik Space.]]
At some point during the [[Kymoodon Era]],<ref name="Author's Cut" /> which lasted from [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]] to [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]],<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Imram, located beyond the frontier of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] at the [[Time/Legends|time]], was [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] by Republic colonists. Members of the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Species/Legends|species]] viewed the world as part of outlying Hutt domains, and the Republic colonization as an act of war. In response, the Hutts backed [[Assault on Imram|raids on Imram]] and other similarly settled worlds that led to the [[Slavery/Legends|enslavement]] or [[Death/Legends|death]] of many colonists.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The events on Imram were later recorded in a [[Belascoan Archive Report|report]] that was prepared as background for a public advisory against [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Rimward]] Republic colonization. The report came to rest in a [[Kymoodon-era government archive|government archive]] on the planet [[Belasco/Legends|Belasco]]. In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], the fragmentary remains of the Belascoan archive report were discovered. This led the [[Academician of Popular Studies]] [[Thunys Albegron]] to [[Proceedings of the Obroa-Skai Conference on Popular Entertainment|mention]] Imram during the [[Obroa-Skai Conference on Popular Entertainment]] a [[6 ABY/Legends|year later]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
Imram was originally meant to be mentioned in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]; however, the sidebar that would have mentioned the world was cut before the book's release. The information regarding Imram was later released in [[2014]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.<ref name="Author's Cut" /> The StarWars.com [[Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion|Online Companion]] to the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Imram system, and therefore the world Imram, in grid square R-13.<ref name="EAOC" />
